why: Each mutant puts back one of the security defects the review found. A green oracle says the fixes are in; these say the oracle would have noticed had they not been. The Unix half of critic-03b — what chmod actually DOES — cannot be swept on this machine, because those cases skip on win32; it is proved by the Linux and macOS CI jobs and the record says so.

mutants.why: the guard falls back to knowing only the dotted spelling, which is the defect: new URL() reports [::ffff:127.0.0.1] as [::ffff:7f00:1], so loopback and cloud metadata become fetchable from a research run
the review found this branch reading the wrong position on a compressed address; the refuse cases for 2002:a9fe::1 and its three siblings are what hold it
the old test refused a..b, ..foo and notes..old, which are legal directory names, and admitted a path on another drive, which is an escape; both halves are now held

the defect inlined rather than named, which is how it would really come back: the file still imports authClientKey, so an oracle asserting only that the old FUNCTION NAME is gone stays green while the two boundaries diverge
the map is keyed by a header the caller sends; that it shrinks shows up in no response, which is why the count is exported at all
the mode argument beside it applies only when the file is created, so dropping the chmod leaves every existing install's log world-readable and nothing else would say so
the directory holds the database and the access token, and a readable directory shows every name in it
SQLite gives -wal and -shm the database's own mode, so this one call is what narrows all three; the reopen after a baseline rebuild is the second and the oracle counts both

mutants.why: the review's blocking finding: narrowing the live database does nothing for the eight whole copies a baseline rebuild and the deploy runner had already left beside it

mutants.why: backupDb copies a whole database on every deploy, before the app has booted and narrowed the source it copies its mode from
the copy is a whole database left beside the live one; that copyFileSync carries the source's mode is libuv behaviour, not a promise this repo makes
this is the fd the server's stdout goes to, and the boot line carries the access token
the token FILE was always 0600; the directory it is minted into was not, and it is the directory that lists what is in it
Dockerfile:16 is COPY . ., so without the exclusion the builder stage takes the local database, its WAL and the auth-token file
critic-05c exists because every signing case used the CH_ name; with only those cases this mutant is invisible, and the PS_ name is the one the documentation gives
same hole on the header half: x-ps-ts and x-ps-signature are documented and were untested
